findings.claim: namesThePartner asks bare matchesText over the whole answer, so a partner alias that is only a word inside the SUBJECT drug's longer name, which every answer about that drug writes, counts as the answer naming her partner order. The completion and findingPartners then go silent for an order the prose never mentioned.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, on 'Can I give her magnesium salicylate?' with an active Salicylic acid order, an answer that names only magnesium salicylate no longer gets 'Also covered by those findings and not named above: active order Salicylic acid.' appended, and findingPartners reads {named:1, stated:1}. This happens because Salicylic acid's rows carry the alias 'salicylate', which matchesText finds inside 'magnesium salicylate'. Base appends the order and reports {1,0}. The same thing happens to the 'penicillin g' order on 'Can I give her procaine benzylpenicillin?' (alias 'benzylpenicillin'). This is a silent fail-open regression on the sentence that exists to name an interacting order the answer left out. It is not the residue the PR declares ('an alias the data files under two substances'): the answer never wrote a shared alias, it wrote the proposed drug's own name. Fix: ask #270's nested-name question, i.e. drop a partner occurrence (DrugReference.namedOccurrences) that sits inside an occurrence of another substance findImpliedByQuery reads in the answer (containedByAny, as substanceOwnsDose and isAboutTheEndedOrderDrug already do), and pin it with a magnesium-salicylate case.
findings.evidence: Throwaway case in CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest, using OverShippedData over the shipped KB through the real search(). Question 'Can I give her magnesium salicylate?', order {Salicylic acid, D01AE12}, model answer 'Magnesium salicylate can be given with caution [4].' At head: coverage {named=1, stated=1}, answer returned unchanged. Same chart and chips with validatorRaising(null, ...), which is containment only and so base semantics: {named=1, stated=0}, and 'Also covered by those findings and not named above: active order Salicylic acid.' is appended. Printed the partner rows DDInter1633/1634/2085: their aliases include 'salicylate' and 'magnesium salicylate tetrahydrate'. Procaine benzylpenicillin with orders Procaine + Benzylpenicillin: head {2,2}, containment {2,1} plus an appended 'active order penicillin g'. A separate KB sweep calling DrugReferenceService.findByQuery on each substance's own name found 79 of 2114 substances whose name also prose-matches another substance's row. That figure says how many names can trigger it, not how many rule pairs are affected. Precedent for the fix: DrugSafetyValidator.substanceOwnsDose (#270, containedByAny at line 13551) and isAboutTheEndedOrderDrug. Reference CLAUDE.md 'Matching a drug name' points to namedOccurrences for #270's sub-span question. Probe edits restored.

findings.claim: The statedPartners javadoc and the ADR Decision 100 amendment say issue #477's findings' orders are 'stated only by its printed name/display'. But statedPartners unions rows across cited findings by printed key, so a #477 order that a co-cited rule finding also prints is stated by the prose rule over that finding's rows.
findings.evidence: Throwaway case, alprazolam over orders {Rifampicin, J04AB02} and {Rifampicin / isoniazid, J04AM02}. The rule finding prints 'Rifampicin / isoniazid' with isoniazid rows, and the #477 finding names [Rifampicin, Rifampicin / isoniazid]. With the #477 finding cited alone, an answer saying 'isoniazid' gives {named=2, stated=1} and appends 'active order Rifampicin / isoniazid'. Co-cited with the rule finding, the #477 order counts as stated and the result is {named=3, stated=3}. The behaviour is defensible because it keeps measure and the append agreeing per key. The two docs should say it (FindingPartnerCoverageCheck.java:268-273, docs/adr.md:7810).

verdict: Not ready to merge: the fix resolves #555's Rifampicin (rifampin) case on all three of its questions, but asking matchesText of the whole answer lets an alias nested inside the proposed drug's own name (magnesium salicylate → Salicylic acid's 'salicylate') silently suppress the 'not named above' completion that base still appends.
what_i_swept: Diff stat checked (15 files, +493/-69, merge-base equals main). Read the PR body, issue #555, the full production diff, and the reference CLAUDE.md in full. Approach (Step 2): prose rule over structurally carried row ids. The siblings namesTheFindingsSubject (#515) and namesTheEndedOrderDrug (PR #478) use the same shape, so the approach is sound, and rejecting the parenthetical strip is consistent with 'Matching a drug name'. Traced outward: every SafetyWarning copy site (with*/as*/aboutSubstance) forwards partnerRows. Every interaction-chip construction site was checked: the drug-in-play arm and the screening arm keys equal namedPartners' partnerName/chipPartnerName, the merge is keyed by member.partnerName, and the question-pair arm names no order. All three LlmInferenceService call sites (search, searchStreaming, module answer) pass the validator. RecordMapping's new getter has no omod reader (zero hits, positive control ChartAnswer = 22 hits). Ran the issue's arrangements plus same-substance and combination-order arrangements end to end through the real search over the shipped KB. Swept the KB for cross-substance prose matches with the real findByQuery and matchesText (calibrated: row 9384 matches 'rifampicin', not 'rifabutin'). Mutated the screening-arm rows: onAScreenOfHerMedications... reddened, which confirms the PR's claim. Ran CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest, FindingPartnerLogDisclosureTest, InteractionClaimPairFidelityTest, ProjectInstructionsGuardTest, SharedMechanismChipCollapseTest, ArchitectureGuardTest, CitationGroundingVerifierTest, LlmInferenceServiceTest and OrderStopDateStatementTest at head: 300 run, 0 failures. Working copy restored and clean.
could_not_verify: No live llama-server/OpenMRS run, so the magnesium-salicylate repro uses a stubbed model answer over the real injector, validator chips and search(). Whether a real model's answer to that question would omit Salicylic acid was not measured.
Did not run the full `mvn clean install`. Only the nine touched/guard test classes listed were run.

The F1 regression was compared against base by running head with a dataset-less validator (containment only, which is identical to base's comparable() containment per the diff), not by building main itself, because the test helpers the probe uses do not exist on main.
notes: Pass 1 found F1 through a KB alias sweep followed by an end-to-end repro. Pass 2 traced copy sites, call sites, wire exposure and the #477 union, which gave F2 (a doc inaccuracy). Pass 3 covered exception handling on the append path (the dataset is already loaded by then) and the performance of getAll() per uncontained partner (2283 rows, negligible) and found nothing substantive. The PR's own claims I checked held: the tests pass and the screening-arm mutation reddens the named case.
